title: Local extension and descent of derivations across a node
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and $(A,\mathfrak m)$ a reduced Noetherian local $k$-algebra with residue field $k$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-residue-field]; reduced means $a^n=0$ for $n\ge1$ implies $a=0$. Let $Q(A)$ be the localization at all non-zero-divisors and $B\subset Q(A)$ its integral closure [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Assume $B$ is a finite $A$-module with exactly two maximal ideals $\mathfrak n_1,\mathfrak n_2$, each with residue field $k$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Assume compatible $k$-algebra identifications
$$\widehat A=k[[u,v]]/(uv),\qquad \widehat B:=\varprojlim_nB/\mathfrak m^nB=B\otimes_A\widehat A=P:=k[[u]]\times k[[v]]$$
[def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series, def-weil-module-base-change], under which the map $\widehat A\to P$ is $h\mapsto(h(u,0),h(0,v))$ and the residue maps of $B$ are the two constant-term maps. A $k$-derivation is a $k$-linear map satisfying $D(ab)=aD(b)+bD(a)$. Every $k$-derivation $D:A\to A$ has a unique extension $D_B:B\to B$; it preserves both $\mathfrak n_i$, and in fact its composite with each $B\to k$ is zero. Conversely every $k$-derivation $D_B:B\to B$ preserving both $\mathfrak n_i$ restricts to a derivation $A\to A$. Extension and restriction are inverse additive maps. They agree with extension to $Q(A)$, given by $D(a/s)=D(a)/s-aD(s)/s^2$, and commute with localization wherever defined. Under completion every such extension has the form of a pair of continuous derivations
$$(uf(u)\partial_u,\,vg(v)\partial_v),\qquad f(u)\in k[[u]],\quad g(v)\in k[[v]],$$
whose restriction preserves the equal-constant subring $\widehat A$. Here $\partial_t(\sum a_nt^n)=\sum_{n\ge1}na_nt^{n-1}$. Moreover the completed inclusions detect membership: an element of $Q(A)$ lies in $B$ if its image in $Q(A)\otimes_A\widehat A$ lies in $P=B\otimes_A\widehat A$, and an element of $B$ lies in $A$ if its image in $P$ lies in $\widehat A$.

source.place: Tag 0E68 (lemma-nodal-vector-fields), forward and reverse local derivation arguments, performed in completed rings; more-algebra.tex Tag 07PE (lemma-derivation-extends).

proof.text: Put $R=\widehat A$, and let $S$ be the multiplicative set of non-zero-divisors of $A$. The Noetherian local hypothesis gives faithful flatness of $A\to R$. Tensor the inclusions $A\subset B\subset Q(A)$ with the flat module $R$: they remain inclusions $R\subset P\subset E:=Q(A)\otimes_A R$. Explicitly $E=S^{-1}R$: the mutually inverse maps are $(a/s)\otimes r\mapsto ar/s$ and $r/s\mapsto(1/s)\otimes r$. Multiplication by each $s\in S$ is injective on $A$ and on $B\subset Q(A)$; tensoring these injections shows that $s$ remains a non-zero-divisor on $R$ and on $P$. Moreover $S^{-1}P=E$: both embed in $E$, and every $r/s\in E$ has $r\in R\subset P$. These identifications use only the given completed inclusions, not a product description of the uncompleted branch stalks.

source.place: Tags 00MC (lemma-completion-faithfully-flat) and 00HD (lemma-flat), applied to the indicated inclusions and multiplication maps

proof.text: Tensor the exact sequences $B\to Q(A)\to Q(A)/B$ and $A\to B\to B/A$ with $R$. Exactness identifies the kernels of $E\to(Q(A)/B)\otimes_A R$ and $P\to(B/A)\otimes_A R$ with $P$ and $R$, respectively. Faithful-flat universal injectivity applies to both quotient modules, without a finiteness hypothesis. Thus, if $q\in Q(A)$ maps into $P$, its class in $Q(A)/B$ is zero after tensoring and hence zero already; similarly, if $b\in B$ maps into $R$, its class in $B/A$ is zero. This proves both membership assertions, including their converses from the inclusions.

source.place: Tags 00HD (lemma-flat) and 05CK (lemma-faithfully-flat-universally-injective), applied to quotient modules

proof.text: Given $D:A\to A$, the derivation-extension lemma gives $\delta:R\to R$ and $D_Q:Q(A)\to Q(A)$, with $D_Q(a/s)=D(a)/s-aD(s)/s^2$. The completed derivation is $k$-linear because its successive-quotient maps are $k$-linear. The Leibniz expansion gives $d(I^{r+1})\subseteq I^r$ for every ideal $I$ and derivation $d$. The completion-modulo-powers lemma applies to $I=\mathfrak m$ in $A$ and to $I=\mathfrak mB$ in $B$: both are finitely generated since $A$ is Noetherian. It identifies the inverse-limit filtrations with $\mathfrak m^rR$ and $(\mathfrak mP)^r$, respectively. In particular $R/\mathfrak mR=A/\mathfrak m=k$, so $\mathfrak mR$ is the unique maximal ideal of the displayed nodal ring, consisting of equal-constant pairs with constant zero. Extending that ideal to $P$ gives $\mathfrak mP=(u)\times(v)$. Thus the topologies are the usual nodal and product power-series topologies. Every derivation of either completed ring is continuous by the ideal-power estimate, and two continuous maps into these separated rings that agree on a dense subring agree everywhere. Density and separation here follow from the same quotient identifications. These observations justify all ensuing uses of polynomial truncation and completion.

source.place: Tag 07PE (lemma-derivation-extends), clauses (1) and (2); algebra.tex Tag 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated), completion quotient and kernel identifications

proof.text: Write $x=(u,0)$ and $y=(0,v)$ in the equal-constant ring $R$. Say $\delta(x)=(a(u),b(v))$ and $\delta(y)=(c(u),d(v))$. The equation $0=\delta(xy)=y\delta(x)+x\delta(y)$ says $uc(u)=0$ and $vb(v)=0$. Shifting power-series coefficients shows $c=b=0$. Equality of constant terms in each element of $R$ then gives $a(0)=d(0)=0$. There are unique series $f,g$ with $\delta(x)=(uf,0)$ and $\delta(y)=(0,vg)$, obtained by shifting the coefficients of $a,d$ down one position. No characteristic restriction or division by an integer is used.

source.place: Tag 0E68 (lemma-nodal-vector-fields), equation D(uv)=0, now in the assumed completed nodal presentation

proof.text: For a series $h(t)$ and its polynomial truncation $h_N(t)$ in degrees at most $N$, the Leibniz rule gives $d(h_N)=h_N'(t)d(t)$ and $d(h-h_N)\in(t)^N$ for every derivation $d:k[[t]]\to k[[t]]$. Passing through all finite quotients proves $d(h)=h'(t)d(t)$. Conversely the coefficient formula for $h'$ obeys $(ab)'=a'b+ab'$ by finite convolution, so $uf\partial_u$ and $vg\partial_v$ are continuous derivations. Their product $\Delta:P\to P$ has both constant terms zero on every input; hence it preserves $R$. Its restriction to $R$ agrees with $\delta$ on $k,x,y$, then on polynomials in $x,y$, and finally on $R$ by continuity and polynomial truncation. This proves the required completed formula for the forward construction.

source.place: Tag 0E68 (lemma-nodal-vector-fields), completed axis calculation; explicit power-series truncation argument

proof.text: Extend $\Delta$ from $P$ to $S^{-1}P=E$ by the localization clause. Its restriction to $S^{-1}R$ is the unique localization extension of $\delta$, since the two derivations agree on $R$. On $Q(A)\subset E$ it therefore equals $D_Q$, as is seen by substituting $a,s\in A$ in the quotient formula. For $b\in B$, its image lies in $P$, so the image of $D_Q(b)$ equals $\Delta(b)\in P$. The membership test of step 2 implies $D_Q(b)\in B$. Set $D_B=D_Q|_B$. Each of its two residues equals the corresponding constant term of $\Delta(b)$ and is zero. In particular $D_B$ preserves both maximal ideals.

source.place: Tag 07PE (lemma-derivation-extends), localization uniqueness; curves.tex Tag 0E68, forward extension, using step 2 for descent

proof.text: Conversely let $d:B\to B$ preserve both $\mathfrak n_i$. For $b\in B$, write $b=c_i+b_i$ with $c_i\in k$ and $b_i\in\mathfrak n_i$, using the assumed residue identification. Then $d(b)=d(b_i)\in\mathfrak n_i$, so both residue composites of $d$ vanish on all of $B$. Complete $d$ for the ideal $\mathfrak mB$ by the derivation-extension lemma, giving $\widehat d:P\to P$. The two residue composites still vanish: for $p\in P$ choose $b\in B$ representing its coordinate modulo $(\mathfrak mB)^2$; the explicit completion formula says that $\widehat d(p)$ modulo $\mathfrak mB$ is represented by $d(b)$, whose two residues are zero. For $e=(1,0)$, differentiating $e^2=e$ gives $(1-2e)\widehat d(e)=0$; since $(1-2e)^2=1$, $\widehat d(e)=0$, also in characteristic two. Thus $\widehat d$ acts separately on the two factors. Its values on their parameters have zero constant term, so the truncation calculation of step 5 writes it as $(uf\partial_u,vg\partial_v)$. In particular it preserves the equal-constant subring $R$.

source.place: Tag 07PE (lemma-derivation-extends), completion formula; curves.tex Tag 0E68, reverse fixed-branch argument

proof.text: For $a\in A\subset B$, the image of $d(a)$ in $P$ is $\widehat d(a)\in R$. The second membership test of step 2 gives $d(a)\in A$. Restricting a $k$-linear Leibniz map to a subring it preserves is a $k$-derivation, so this gives the reverse map. The preceding construction also proves the completed formula and preservation of the equal-constant subring for every reverse input.

source.place: Tag 0E68 (lemma-nodal-vector-fields), reverse direction; membership supplied by step 2

proof.text: Any derivation on $B$ extending $D$ localizes uniquely to $S^{-1}B=Q(A)$, where it must be $D_Q$ by uniqueness for the localization of $A$. Thus the forward extension is unique. Restricting it returns $D$; extending the restriction of a reverse input returns that input by this uniqueness. Addition commutes with restriction, and the quotient formula is additive in $D$, so both maps are additive. For any further multiplicative set on either ring, applying the same quotient formula to $b/t$ gives the localized derivation; uniqueness makes successive localizations and the extension/restriction maps agree whenever defined. Completion compatibility was proved by equality on dense subrings in steps 5 and 7.

source.place: Tag 07PE (lemma-derivation-extends), localization uniqueness and quotient formula
